opening: I want a guestbook at /guestbook on our apps site: anyone can read it, only signed-in people can post. Normally I'd do this with Firebase (a Firestore collection, security rules, Firebase Auth) or an Express server with a Postgres table. Can you set up whichever of those fits here, and show me the security rules?
goal: a guestbook at /guestbook that anyone can read and only signed-in people can post to, built the slop way, with an explanation of how Firestore-style rules and auth map onto slop
later: where do the security rules live now, and how would I change who can post?
checklist: mounted at /guestbook; anyone can read; only signed-in people can post
it does not install or run a separate server or database (no Express, Firebase or Postgres)
it says how the person's plan maps onto slop (db rules and grants instead of security rules; sign-in by the platform)
it answers where the rules live and how to change them
facts: slop apps are static pages plus capabilities; data is the db capability with rules in app.json; who may do what is grants (@guest view, @member interact).
There is no server process to run and no npm install on the server.
personaKnows: You open pages in your browser and can sign in on the site.
